page:
Codecs for bidirectional transformations between input and output types introduced in zod@4.1. Sharing single schema across network boundaries for converting JSON-friendly formats to rich JavaScript representations. Forward parsing (input→output) and backward encoding (output→input).
- Codecs as special schema types with bidirectional transformations
- z.codec(inputSchema, outputSchema, {decode, encode})
- .parse and .decode for forward transformation (input→output)
- z.decode for strongly-typed input (unlike .parse with unknown)
- .encode for backward transformation (output→input)
- z.invertCodec to swap input/output and directions
- Network boundary conversion between JSON and JavaScript types
- Codec subtypes as pipes with interstitial transform logic
- How do codecs work for data transformation?
- When should I use codecs instead of transforms?
- How do I encode/decode with a codec?
- What are common codec implementations?

sections.manifest: How encoding works in Zod schemas and codec subtypes. Codecs encapsulate bidirectional transformations with decode and encode functions. Pipes chain schemas (forward: A→B, backward: B→A). Refinements execute both directions. Transforms are unidirectional (error if encountered during encode). Stringbool internally implemented as codec. Defaults/prefaults and .catch only apply forward. Mutating transforms (.trim, .toLowerCase) work both directions.

Commonly-needed codec implementations. stringToNumber (parseFloat), stringToInt (parseInt), stringToBigInt (BigInt), numberToBigInt. Date conversions: isoDatetimeToDate, epochSecondsToDate, epochMillisToDate. JSON parsing with error handling. Byte conversions: utf8ToBytes, bytesToUtf8, base64ToBytes, base64urlToBytes, hexToBytes. URL: stringToURL, stringToHttpURL. URI component encoding/decoding. All provided as copy/paste implementations for customization.
